trigger: A technician live-cert stage, repair command, validator, manifest, schema, CMD launcher, report, exact-next-command handoff, or scoped skill changes.
A field failure contradicts static or CI evidence.
An operator command includes a shell prompt, duplicated prompt, continuation prompt, transcript, stack trace, or PowerShell diagnostic output.
A new Windows PowerShell or PowerShell 7 compatibility boundary is introduced.

actions: Read AGENTS.md, the selected skill, scoped codebase map, scoped manifest, operator-command contract, and current operator evidence.
Run git status --short, git branch --show-current, and git log --oneline --decorate -5 without a pager.
Separate executable input from the operator's prompt, output, and error transcript before attempting reproduction.
Preserve unrelated work and use an isolated branch or worktree when another writer owns the checkout.
phases.gate: Repository identity, ownership, exact shell, sanitized command, and failure boundary are recorded.

actions: Classify each requirement as reuse, extend, repair, retire, or create.
Keep operator behavior in stage/repair code, reusable procedure in scoped skills, deterministic command presentation in the operator-command contract, and proof in validators/artifacts.
Prefer a repository-owned CMD or PS1 entrypoint over a long inline bootstrap.
Reject prompt-only, documentation-only, or visual-review-only fixes for executable or command-presentation defects.
phases.gate: One canonical owner exists for every changed behavior, command surface, and artifact.

actions: Repair the defect and add a behavior-level or executable compatibility guard.
For command contamination, add or update a minimized synthetic fixture and require a sanitized replacement command.
Update the scoped map, registry, workflow, skill, report, or CI when the change affects those contracts.
Keep generated evidence outside tracked paths and keep private operator transcripts out of fixtures.
phases.gate: The owned vertical slice is complete, fixture-backed, and no duplicate implementation exists.

actions: Run the operator-command envelope Python and PowerShell validators.
Run focused Python tests.
Run the surface and harness validators in Windows PowerShell 5.1.
Run the same validators in PowerShell 7.
Validate any candidate handoff artifact with -CandidatePath.
Run CMD fixture-safe dispatch and git --no-pager diff --check.
Run broader repository validation only after focused checks pass.
phases.gate: Every required shell, fixture, registered command surface, and focused validator passes at the exact candidate HEAD.

actions: Record files changed, validator results, proof ceiling, commit SHA, push/PR state, preserved local work, and the exact next command.
Name the shell, owner, dependency, expected artifact, and completion gate outside the command block.
Put executable input only inside the command block; omit prompts, output, transcript text, and expected results.
When runtime proof remains, name the workstation stage and artifact that advances it.
Do not claim live behavior from CI.
phases.gate: A fresh agent can resume without reconstructing the failure, editing a transcript-shaped command, or guessing the validation order.

failureHandling.correctableFailure: Repair in the same branch and rerun the complete affected gate.
failureHandling.operatorCommandContamination: Preserve the original privately, classify it with the fixture-backed validator, publish only the sanitized command, and add a synthetic fixture when the signature is new.
failureHandling.environmentBlocker: Record the exact shell, command, exit code, evidence path, and owned repair command.
failureHandling.collision: Stop mutation, preserve both branches/worktrees, and assign one convergence owner.
failureHandling.proofContradiction: Observed field failure outranks lower proof and remains blocking until exact-command rerun.

forbidden: private usernames or hostnames in fixtures
runtime proof promotion from hosted CI
shell prompts or transcript text in executable handoff blocks
